title: Longview’s October 8 Agenda Seeks $1.29 Million for 26 Replacement Vehicles
seoTitle: Longview Seeks $1.29 Million for Fleet Replacements
summary: Longview’s October 8 agenda seeks up to $1,292,718.63 for 26 replacement vehicles. The packet identifies the purchasing routes, budget limits and a cooperative-reference discrepancy.
content:
Longview City Council’s October 8 agenda includes two proposed fleet purchases with a combined ceiling of $1,292,718.63 for 26 replacement vehicles. The city posted the agenda October 2. These are requests for council authorization; they are not evidence that the purchases have been approved or paid.

The meeting is scheduled for 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, 300 West Cotton Street. The vehicle items appear on the consent agenda, with citizen comment listed earlier in the meeting.

## What the city proposes to buy

Item E seeks up to $989,524.63 for nine 2027 Chevrolet Tahoes and eleven 2027 Ford Explorers from Sames Laredo Chevrolet / Sames Bastrop Ford. Item F seeks up to $303,194 for four 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 4WD vehicles and two 2027 Ford F-150s from Caldwell Country Chevrolet/Ford. Adding the two listed ceilings produces the $1.29 million total.

The master packet identifies the Vehicle Replacement Fund account for both requests. Staff say the vehicles would replace units at the end of their useful service lives. Both draft resolutions would require purchases to fit the 2026–27 budget without an amendment.

## The purchasing route matters

The SUV request uses The Interlocal Purchasing System, or TIPS; the pickup request uses TASB BuyBoard. Staff describe both as cooperative purchases and say the equipment was competitively bid through those cooperatives. That is the city’s stated procurement basis, rather than a finding by RepWatchr that every contractual requirement has been satisfied.

The short agenda refers to Region VII for TIPS, while the detailed staff report and draft resolution refer to Region VIII. Readers should know about that discrepancy. The city should clarify the correct cooperative reference before executing documents. The mismatch alone does not establish wrongdoing.

## What to check after the meeting

A spending ceiling is only the starting point for accountability. The useful follow-up records are the adopted resolutions, vote record, executed purchase orders and final invoices. Those documents can show whether the requests passed, what the city actually ordered and how much it ultimately paid.

A clear replacement schedule should also identify the outgoing vehicles, their mileage, maintenance costs and disposal plans. Those are questions for follow-up reporting; this article does not claim that the vehicles are unnecessary or that their prices are excessive.

Residents can inspect the linked packet before the meeting. Longview’s council-meeting page links to live and on-demand viewing and its agenda center. Check the current agenda again before attending in case the city posts a revision.

This report was checked October 2, 2026. RepWatchr will update the article after the council’s decision and supporting records become available.
